column1: # Diet method dishes (diet-food-words/3): the dishes and preparations the book recipes of the corpus are named for (pye, patty, fricassee, ragout, croquette), derived from the corpus, never listed by hand (review ck16-2 and ck16-4: 68410's method makes "a pye" no line carries, 133979's "a garnish of rizotto"). A book method that names one where no line of its recipe carries it names a dish the lines do not list, so a severe type holds the recipe as unknown when it does not understand the word: a shape of the catalog the set would read as clear (DietFoodWords.FormKind.Shape: "fill the patties"), or a dish form or a word no curated food knows as more than a prepared mixture's unless the recipe's own title names it (the fricassee a "Fricassee of Chicken" makes, and the pudding of a "Rice Pudding", are made of its lines).

# Derivation, on the read-only staging copy of 2026-11-25: for every live book recipe (DietRecipeText.FromBook), the last food word of its title (DietFoodWords.Words of DietRecipeText.Title) and the words of its method (DietFoodWords.MethodWords of DietRecipeText.Sentences); a word is kept when it ends the titles of at least 3 book recipes and those titles are at least two fifths of the book recipes whose method names it (below that the word is a vessel or a step far more often than a dish: casserole, timbale, mould, saute, boil).
# titles: the book recipes whose title ends with the word; methods: the book recipes whose method names it.
